questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most important was that my destination was a spanish speaking place. Further, it was important that the university is recognised as a quality institution with good facilities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy and the guy in charge of helping exchange students do an extremely good job whenever you have doubts.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had information days where we were told everything more than one time, so it is difficult to miss the important information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it after a little research. Most of the time I lived in Livinnx 18 which was very good. It has a gym, laundry and a terrace with an amazing view over town and the mountains. Also a lot of students from Uniandes lived there. It was a bit expensive though, so the last part of the stay I moved to a house called VillaVerde that is also close to campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Choose a place close to campus as the long commutes everyday will get you tired.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I needed to fill out a lot of forms, but take a deep breath - you will make it through the bureaucracy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I would say that the thing that helped me was sending emails to people that have the answers whenever in doubt.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all my desired classes

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look deeply into the courses as the quality varied a lot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It varied a lot. Overall I had pretty good courses, but some of my friends had other stories. Off course it depends a lot on the teacher, so look up what former students have written.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I would say that in Uniandes I listened more to the teacher than I was used to, due to fewer student involving activities. But at the same time, the teachers ask a lot of open questions in the classroom, so an engaged student would definitely have the opportunity to participate.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Spanish for foreigners (ELE 3)
Escalada del muro
Natacion
Cultura y Naturaleza
Ceramica basica

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Cultura y Naturaleza is a very good social sciences course about what is cultural and what is natural. Florencia is a very engaged teacher and I can only recommend it.

I had ceramics and I'm very happy that I chose it. See if you can choose the one with Nubia as a teacher. There is no homework and no exam so it's a great pause from the academics to challenge your creative self. I loved it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Some very specific things was more expensive than anticipated. For example good cheese or a good duve to sleep with. So, I would recommend to go with the local goods, for example fruit and vegetables are very cheap. Also, a lot of places serve menu of the day which is always extremely cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The sports center is amazing. Take some sports classes if you have time. Or just take the open dancing classes. There is amazing facilities, as for example swimming pool, climbing wall, volleyball field, gym and so on.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Salsa, swimming etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the north of town and see how different it is. Also, try to find a local that lives in the south to take you on a tour in the neighbourhoods, but choose somebody you trust - it is kind of dangerous alone.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Use the 'hermanos sin fronteras' group. It is a group of students that voluntarily help exchange students. They are super nice and a good way in to meeting locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the security issue. You have to be carefull after dark and always pair up with others.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and helpfullness of complete strangers. Everybody wants to talk to you and help you without anything in return. As an example, my barber took me to his neighbourhood to show me around and meet his family and friends without expecting nothing in return.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bring hot clothing and maybe rain clothing as Bogota is colder and wetter than you would think. 
Learn how to dance salsa if you want to be a big hit with the locals.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: xx

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Meeting new people, both locals and foreigners.
Going around Colombia for extended weekend trips. It is a country with extreme diversity from rivers, to volcanos, mountains, jungle, ocean and all with different cultures, foods and colours.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Improving my spanish as people don't speak English. But also a good motivation to actually speak spanish.
